title: anchore_api_credential data block
description: The `data` block of an `anchore_api_credential` secret consumed by the Anchore collector (req-anchore-connection). One envelope per Anchore instance and account: the connection settings sit beside the credential so that editing a second file cannot redirect it. Owned by the anchore plugin and validated by the collector before any request. The credential must be a READ-ONLY Anchore role for the named account; an admin credential must not be used. Strict: only the fields of the named scheme are allowed.

base_url.description: The Anchore API root including /v2, for example https://anchore.example:8228/v2 for an on-prem install or the hosted service's /v2 root. The scheme is whatever is written here, http or https, and is never changed; a plain http root sends the credential and every response unencrypted, and every run says so. No userinfo, no query, no fragment, no trailing slash.

account.description: The Anchore account this credential reads. Required, and part of every key the collector writes. Sent as the x-anchore-account header where the instance needs it.

ca_bundle.description: Absolute path of a PEM file on the host holding the CA certificates to trust for this instance, for a private CA. The path, never the file's contents. Certificate verification is never turned off.

annotation_allowlist.description: Annotation keys that may be stored from Anchore. Empty by default: no annotation key is stored unless it is listed.

scheme.description: Which authentication scheme this credential uses. It selects the credential fields below and admits no others.

username.description: scheme basic only: the Anchore user name. A read-only user.

password.description: scheme basic only: that user's password. Never printed, logged, or placed in a URL.

key.description: scheme api_key only: the Anchore API key. It is sent as the password of the documented user name _api_key. Never printed, logged, or placed in a URL.

token.description: scheme bearer only: an OAuth2 bearer token already minted and held here. The client never calls a token endpoint, because obtaining a token is a POST. Minting and renewing it is the operator's, out of band. Never printed, logged, or placed in a URL.
